title: Screen-reader validation feedback and group-naming fixes on duty-to-accommodate intake

history.detail:
CONDITIONAL: CONDITIONAL PASS â€” QA1 audit round 1, Sprint 9, commit 4e03bad, HEAD, clean for every file under audit. Sprint file re-read fresh in full immediately before recording this verdict (blob unmodified in the worktree; the only dirty path in the tree is sprint-7's definition, unrelated to this sprint). SCOPE LIMIT, STATED UP FRONT PER THE SPRINT'S OWN GATE-1 CRITERION I do not verify that any of this is announced. Everything below is attribute correctness, ID resolution, and diff scope. Audibility is gate 3, Chang's NVDA pass. Nothing in this audit should be read as confirming how anything sounds. =================================================================== THE FIVE MECHANICAL CHECKS â€” ALL PASS =================================================================== 1. DIFF SCOPE â€” PASS. Code diff is one file, components/IntakeFlow.tsx, +3/-12. The other three paths in the commit are sprint bookkeeping (the sprint file, registry.json, state/sprint-9.json). Verified by explicit path filters that lib/, app/ and every test path are untouched: no validation predicate, no visibility rule (visibleProceduralQuestions is not in the diff), no domain type, and grep across the diff for legend=/OPTIONS/helperText= returns nothing, so no question wording moved. Requirement 4 satisfied. 2. REQUIREMENT 3 STATEMENT PRESENT â€” PASS as to presence. Dev Notes carries a named per-round analysis for rounds 3, 4 and 5. The diff is auditable. Two of the three arguments are defective; see ISSUES 2 and 3 â€” that is a soundness problem, not an absence, so it is not the automatic FAIL this criterion reserves for a diff with no statement at all. 3. aria-describedby TARGETS RESOLVE, aria-invalid ON A SUPPORTING ROLE â€” PASS. Two referenced IDs, both guarded by the same condition that renders them: - helperId (IntakeFlow.tsx:631) is composed into describedBy only when helperText is truthy, and the

renders under the same truthiness test. Cannot dangle. - dutyToAccommodateErrorId (IntakeFlow.tsx:715) is passed as describedById by all four call sites only when dutyToAccommodateError is non-null (767, 778, 790, 800), and the

renders under {dutyToAccommodateError && ...} (804-806). Same predicate on both sides, so the reference and the target appear and disappear together. - describedBy collapses to undefined when both are absent, so no empty aria-describedby="" is emitted. aria-invalid sits on role="radiogroup", which supports it per ARIA 1.2. Confirmed independently rather than taken from Dev Notes: jsx-a11y/role-supports-aria-props is actually active in this project's resolved ESLint config (verified via --print-config; it comes in through eslint-config-next at warn level), and `eslint components/IntakeFlow.tsx` exits 0 with no output. The rule is on and silent, not absent. Per-question invalid predicates (717-722) are each scoped to their own answer, so an answered group is not flagged alongside an unanswered one. That property is preserved from Sprint 8. 4. EXACTLY ONE NAMED ELEMENT PER GROUP â€” PASS. Swept the whole file: there is no aria-labelledby and no aria-label anywhere in components/IntakeFlow.tsx, and role="radiogroup" appears exactly once (636), on the fieldset. The nested div is now className-only. One accessible object per group, named by its own , which is the first element child. The round-5 two-object structure that produced NVDA finding 1 is genuinely gone. This is the check the sprint asked for and it passes. 5. VITEST GREEN, NO RENDER-ASSERTION TEST ADDED â€” PASS. `npx vitest run`: 14 files, 63/63 passing, matching Dev Notes' claim exactly. No test file appears in the diff at all, so no render assertion could have been added. package.json and the vitest config contain no jsdom, happy-dom, or @testing-library entry. Requirement 6's "markup-only, no new pure function, stated in Dev Notes" route is taken correctly: describedBy's composition is unchanged, only the element it renders onto moved, so there is no new decision to test. =================================================================== ISSUES FOUND =================================================================== 1. [HIGH â€” the required fix] The diff restores the exact markup configuration GroundTruth measured as nameless, and takes neither remediation it offered. components/IntakeFlow.tsx:636. The new element is byte-for-byte the structure round 3 removed:

with no aria-label and no aria-labelledby. That is probe B in GroundTruth's Sprint 8 round-1 calibration, recorded verbatim in sprint-8.json: B role="radiogroup" + BRAVOLEGEND -> radiogroup, NO NAME C role="radiogroup" + aria-label="CHARLIEARIALABEL" -> NAME SHOWN D role="radiogroup" + aria-labelledby -> legend -> NO NAME GroundTruth's own reading of that: C proves the instrument can see a radiogroup name when one exists, so B's silence is "meaningful signal rather than a null result"; D proves the instrument under-reports, so B's silence is "NOT proof of an empty computed name." Unresolved in both directions, which is why it closed CONDITIONAL rather than FAIL. GroundTruth then offered two fixes and said why there were two: "(a) Drop the redundant role=radiogroup ... (b) Keep the role and add aria-labelledby pointing at the legend's id. Either makes the name correct under every implementation, so nobody has to resolve which reading of my evidence is right." Round 3 took (a). This diff takes neither. It restores the one configuration whose name has never been confirmed by any instrument, and it does so on the sprint whose requirement 2 is that the accessible name must remain the full question text. I am not asserting the name is absent â€” I can't, and neither could anyone else in this project's history. I am asserting the diff leaves a previously-measured, still-unresolved risk in place when one attribute removes it. Option (b) is available and costs nothing here: restore the useId legendId and add aria-labelledby={legendId} to the same fieldset. That does NOT reintroduce finding 1. The double announcement came from two accessible objects (outer native fieldset + inner aria-labelledby'd div), not from two naming mechanisms on one object. One element is one accessible object with one name, however that name is sourced, and aria-labelledby simply makes the source deterministic instead of dependent on whether native legend naming survives a role override. Rounds 4 and 5 stay satisfied: aria-invalid still sits on role="radiogroup", and aria-invalid plus aria-describedby plus the name remain on one element together. The alternative â€” ship as-is and let gate 3 settle it â€” is not unreasonable on its face, since Chang's NVDA setup now works and would catch a silent name. I am rejecting it because this sprint's own Risks section says the requirement-3 analysis exists "so it fails the audit rather than the retro," and because a gate-3 round spends the one resource the Dependencies section names as scarce and external: a human's availability. Spending an NVDA session to answer a question a one-line attribute makes unaskable is the wrong trade. 2. [MEDIUM] Dev Notes misattributes the calibration evidence and reverses its chronology. Sprint 9 file, Dev Notes, round 3 paragraph. It reads: "QA1's own round-2 audit (recorded on Sprint 8) later ran a calibration control through that same instrument and found it under-reports aria-labelledby-derived names too." The calibration was GroundTruth's, not mine, run as CONTROL 2 in the round-1 live test. Timestamps in sprint-8.json: my round-2 audit is 2026-08-19T06:15:44Z; GroundTruth's calibration is 2026-08-21T20:02:09Z. It came two days after my audit, not "later" than round 3 by way of my audit. My round-2 audit contains no calibration probe and never touched an accessibility-tree instrument â€” I don't open browsers. The conclusion drawn from it survives the correction: GroundTruth did prove under-reporting via probe D and did decline to call B a proven defect. But requirement 3 makes this analysis an audited written deliverable, and an audit trail that credits the wrong role and inverts the order sends the next person to a document that doesn't contain the evidence. Fix the attribution. 3. [MEDIUM] The round-3 rebuttal's supporting argument is a non-sequitur, and it is load-bearing. Sprint 9 file, Dev Notes, round 3 paragraph. It argues the name will be fine because "the same native fieldset+legend naming path is used elsewhere in this file (Step 1's employment-status and formal-complaints fieldsets) and was not flagged as silent by this pass." Those fieldsets carry no role override â€” IntakeFlow.tsx:418, 454 and 515 are bare
. Whether native legend naming survives role="radiogroup" is the entire question, and a bare fieldset is the control that holds that variable at the opposite value. GroundTruth already made this exact point in round 1: " is a fieldset-specific naming mechanism, defined for the group role that
maps to natively. role=radiogroup overrides that mapping, and legend-to-name support for the overridden role is inconsistent across engines." The companion argument has the same shape. Dev Notes says the NVDA pass "confirms names are announced by the shipped (round-5) pattern, just twice." True, and it cuts the other way: in round 5 the outer fieldset had NO role override, so what NVDA confirmed is that a bare fieldset's legend announces. No configuration Chang tested had role="radiogroup" on a fieldset. The pass provides no evidence about the element this diff creates. 4. [LOW â€” no action required] The fieldset's aria-describedby now points at helperId, a

that is its own descendant (636 referencing 639). Legal, and round 5's helper-text wiring is preserved as Dev Notes claims. Noting only that the helper text is now both the group's description and content encountered inside it, so some AT will surface it twice in one pass. That is a gate-3 observation if it matters at all, not a defect I'm blocking on. =================================================================== RECOMMENDATION =================================================================== Two required fixes before this goes to Pipeman: A. Make the accessible name deterministic. Apply GroundTruth's option (b): reinstate the legendId useId, put aria-labelledby={legendId} on the single fieldset at 636, keep everything else exactly as it is. If Dev Team would rather defend the current markup, the alternative is an authoritative accname measurement of THIS configuration â€” AOM-enabled Chrome, CDP getPartialAXTree, or a screen reader â€” not an inference from bare fieldsets elsewhere in the file. B. Correct the two defective justifications in Dev Notes (issues 2 and 3). Requirement 3 made this analysis auditable on purpose; it has to be right, not merely present. The round-3 rebuttal's honest form is: round 3's finding rested on an instrument GroundTruth itself showed under-reports, no authoritative measurement of either configuration has ever been taken, and this sprint therefore makes the name explicit rather than relying on either round's unverified assumption. Everything else in this diff is clean. The collapse to one accessible object is the right structural call and it is implemented correctly â€” the scope discipline is exact, the ID guards are symmetric, the per-question invalid predicates survived intact, and nobody tried to smuggle in a render test to prove the markup. Fix A and B and re-audit; this is one attribute and one paragraph away from a PASS. Re-audit note: the sprint file changes under fix B, which is expected and fine at this phase â€” no PASS has recorded a file hash yet, so nothing is invalidated.

PASS: PASS â€” QA1 audit round 2, Sprint 9, commit 011647a (HEAD), audited paths clean in the worktree. Sprint file re-read fresh in full before recording; it changed since round 1 (Dev Notes revised under item B, which is what I asked for), and I audited against the amended text, not my round-1 copy. The only dirty path in the tree is sprint-7's definition, unrelated to this sprint. Both round-1 items are closed. Focused re-audit per the agent file's guidance on small isolated amendments: the code delta from 4e03bad is +7/-8 in one file and I re-ran every gate-1 check against it rather than carrying forward round 1's results. SCOPE LIMIT, UNCHANGED AND STILL LOAD-BEARING I do not verify that any of this is announced. What follows is attribute correctness, ID resolution, object count as determined by markup, and diff scope. Whether NVDA speaks the name once, and speaks the invalid state and error text on entry to a failed group, is gate 3 and remains entirely open. Nothing here should be read as evidence about how any of it sounds. =================================================================== ITEM A â€” CLOSED =================================================================== components/IntakeFlow.tsx:637-645. The fieldset now carries role="radiogroup", aria-labelledby={legendId}, aria-invalid={invalid} and aria-describedby together, with as its first element child. This is GroundTruth's option (b) applied exactly as offered in its Sprint 8 round-1 report. STILL ONE ACCESSIBLE OBJECT, NOT TWO. Confirmed by full-file sweep, not by reading Dev Notes: role="radiogroup" appears exactly once in components/IntakeFlow.tsx (638), aria-labelledby appears exactly once (639), and aria-label appears nowhere. The inner
remains className-only. Step 1's three fieldsets (418, 454, 515) are still bare and were not touched by this diff. The reasoning that matters, stated so the next auditor does not have to re-derive it: one element is one accessible object with one accessible name, regardless of how many naming mechanisms point at it. accname resolves aria-labelledby ahead of host-language native naming, so the name is now the legend text by explicit reference, with the native fieldset/legend path pointing at the same text on the same object as a fallback. Finding 1's mechanism â€” an outer native fieldset and a separate inner radiogroup both surfacing the same string as two objects â€” is structurally impossible in this markup, because there is no second object to surface anything. THE ROUND-1 CONCERN IS RESOLVED, NOT DEFERRED. My CONDITIONAL was not that the name was proven absent; it was that 4e03bad restored probe B â€” the one configuration whose name no instrument has ever confirmed â€” while a one-attribute change made the question unaskable. That change is now made. Both surviving naming paths resolve to the same string on the same element, so the computed name cannot be empty on any engine, whichever mechanism it honours. That is the strongest position static review can reach here, and it is reached without spending a gate-3 session to answer it. aria-labelledby's target cannot dangle: renders unconditionally, with no truthiness guard, and useId() yields a distinct id per component instance, so the four groups cannot collide. =================================================================== ITEM B â€” CLOSED, BOTH HALVES =================================================================== ATTRIBUTION CORRECTED, AND CORRECT. Dev Notes now reads: the "no accessible name" finding was "reported in GroundTruth's round-1 live test on Sprint 8 (CONDITIONAL) â€” which ran *after* QA1's round-2 PASS on Sprint 8, not before," with the calibration described as "that same live test's own calibration controls (five fieldsets injected into the live page) ... (control D)." Checked against sprint-8.json rather than accepted on its face. Right actor: the calibration is CONTROL 2 inside GroundTruth's live_test event. Right ordering: QA1 round-2 PASS at 2026-08-19T06:15:44Z, GroundTruth round-1 live test at 2026-08-21T20:02:09Z. Right control: D is the aria-labelledby probe that demonstrated under-reporting. The claim that my round-2 audit ran a calibration is gone from the file entirely â€” grep for "QA1's own round-2" returns nothing. THE STEP 1 COMPARISON IS GONE, NOT SOFTENED. grep across the whole sprint file for "Step 1", "employment-status" and "formal-complaints" returns nothing. The argument was deleted rather than hedged, which is the correct outcome â€” it was invalid, not merely overstated. THE COMPANION CLAIM IS ALSO FIXED, WHICH I ASKED FOR AND WOULD HAVE CHECKED ANYWAY. The NVDA sentence now ends: "evidence about the *two-object* structure, not about whether a single role='radiogroup' element with aria-labelledby announces correctly, which this revision does not further assume either way." That is the honest scope of Chang's pass. Dev Team went further than the letter of item B here and correctly declined to claim evidence it does not have. The revised round-3 paragraph now argues the right thing: the instrument is not fully reliable either way, and "not fully reliable" is not a licence to omit the explicit name. That is a sound reading of the record instead of a rebuttal built on a bad comparison. =================================================================== THE FIVE GATE-1 CHECKS, RE-RUN AGAINST 011647a =================================================================== 1. DIFF SCOPE â€” PASS. Against Sprint 8's close (bf91df8), the entire code delta is components/IntakeFlow.tsx, +7/-8. Path-filtered diffs of lib/, app/, package.json and the vitest config are empty. No validation predicate, no visibleProceduralQuestions(), no domain type, and no legend=/OPTIONS/helperText= string moved. Requirement 4 satisfied. 2. REQUIREMENT 3 STATEMENT â€” PASS, on substance this time. Rounds 3, 4 and 5 each still have a named paragraph, and the round-3 one is now sound. Rounds 4 and 5 were not edited and did not need to be: round 4's constraint (aria-invalid on an element with role="radiogroup") still holds, and round 5's "don't split name, validity and description across nodes" is not merely preserved but strengthened â€” all four attributes now sit on one element, which is what that principle wanted. 3. aria-describedby TARGETS RESOLVE, aria-invalid ON A SUPPORTING ROLE â€” PASS. helperId is composed into describedBy only when helperText is truthy and the

renders under the same test. dutyToAccommodateErrorId is passed by all four call sites only when dutyToAccommodateError is non-null, and its

renders under the same predicate. describedBy collapses to undefined when both are absent, so no empty attribute is emitted. aria-invalid sits on role="radiogroup", which supports it per ARIA 1.2; jsx-a11y/role-supports-aria-props is active in the resolved config and `eslint components/IntakeFlow.tsx` exits 0 silent on the revised markup. Per-question invalid predicates remain scoped to their own answer. 4. NO ELEMENT NAMED TWICE â€” PASS. Covered under item A above. 5. VITEST GREEN, NO RENDER-ASSERTION TEST â€” PASS. 14 files, 63/63, unchanged. No test file appears anywhere in the diff. No jsdom, happy-dom or @testing-library in package.json or the vitest config. Requirement 6's markup-only route still applies: describedBy's composition is untouched and the revision adds no branch or decision. =================================================================== ISSUES FOUND =================================================================== None blocking. Two notes, neither requiring action: 1. [LOW, carried forward] The fieldset's aria-describedby still points at helperId, its own descendant. Legal, and round 5's wiring is preserved. Some AT may surface the helper text both as the group's description and as content inside it. A gate-3 observation if it matters at all; I flagged it in round 1 and it has not changed. 2. [INFORMATIONAL] Dev Notes retains the self-verification block for 4e03bad alongside a new one for the revision, each labelled with its commit. That is the right call â€” the superseded evidence stays legible as superseded rather than being silently overwritten. =================================================================== RECOMMENDATION =================================================================== Ships. Gate 1 is closed. Two things Dev Team and Pipeman need to know before this moves: 1. DO NOT EDIT THE SPRINT FILE BETWEEN THIS PASS AND /sprint-dev-done. This PASS records a hash of the file as audited, and dev_done refuses outright, no override, if it changes. If the file must change, re-audit first â€” that refusal is the check working, not an obstacle to route around. 2. THIS DIFF IS ARIA. Per CLAUDE.md, if GroundTruth returns FAIL or CONDITIONAL and the fix touches ARIA attributes, roles, labels or accessible names, that fix gets an independent QA1 review of the diff, recorded in Dev Notes, before Pipeman reships â€” not the fast reship path. Sprint 8 round 3 introduced a fresh ARIA regression and was caught only because QA1 happened still to be in the loop. That was luck; this is the control. And the standing reminder, because it is the whole point of this sprint: gate 1 and gate 2 passing means the markup is right, not that it is audible. Requirements 1, 2 and 5 are settled by Chang's NVDA pass across all four questions â€” documentationTiming included, which has still never been through an AT pass â€” and by nothing else. Closing this sprint without gate 3 recorded in Dev Notes verifies nothing it was created to verify. The work is clean. Both items were fixed properly rather than argued around, and the one place Dev Team could have overclaimed â€” what Chang's pass actually covers â€” it explicitly declined to. That is the right instinct.
